questions.question: Which statement about JPA and Hibernate is correct?
options: Hibernate is a specification, and JPA is a library that implements it
They are two names for the same JAR file
JPA is a specification, and Hibernate is a library that implements it
JPA works only with MySQL, and Hibernate works only with H2
questions.explanation: JPA is only the set of rules. Hibernate is the provider that follows them and does the real work.

questions.question: A monthly sales report needs several joins and a group by. Which tool usually fits best?
options: Hand-written SQL through JdbcClient
Only save() and findAll() from a repository
Editing the entity annotations at runtime
Reading the whole table into a list and looping in Java
questions.explanation: Reports with joins and grouping are clearer and faster as SQL, and JdbcClient runs it with little code.

questions.question: The app saves CakeOrder("Chocolate", 1.5) with the repository, then prints repository.findAll() using the toString shown in the code. What is printed?
options: CakeOrder[null, Chocolate, 1.5 kg]
Chocolate 1.5
Nothing, because findAll needs a query
CakeOrder[1, Chocolate, 1.5 kg]
questions.explanation: With IDENTITY, the database gives the first row id 1, and findAll returns the stored entity.

questions.question: An entity has only a constructor that takes two arguments and no empty constructor. Hibernate fails to load rows. Why?
options: Entities may never have any constructor
Hibernate needs a no-argument constructor to create entity objects
The constructor must be private and static
Hibernate only works with records
questions.explanation: Hibernate creates entity objects itself and then fills the fields, so it needs a no-argument constructor.

questions.question: A developer adds only the plain jakarta.persistence API and no provider, then expects save() to work. What is wrong?
options: The save method was removed in Spring Boot 4
JPA is only a contract, so a provider such as Hibernate must be on the classpath
H2 cannot be used with JPA
The class needs an @Service annotation
questions.explanation: The API has no working code. The Spring Boot data starter pulls in Hibernate, which supplies it.
